title: Redispatchable attribution for embeddings/rerank-triggered external tool executions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Batched embeddings + rerank workloads often fan out to per-candidate tool executions (external scoring, retrieval, or structured function calls). When requests are retried, speculatively prefetched, or redistributed across workers due to rate caps, customers are seeing overcharges or inconsistent quota consumption. Current metering charges each worker-executed toolcall at execution time, which leads to double-billing in the face of redispatch and opaque refunds when partial executions are cancelled by rate-limits. This is especially visible for large batched reranks (100s-1k candidates) where only a subset of tool calls are required for final scoring, but speculative execution occurs for latency reasons.

Scope: Design and implement a redispatchable attribution model for embeddings/rerank-triggered tool executions and structured outputs on non-chat endpoints. The model should: (1) attribute provisional credits at request admission, (2) associate a per-request trace token across worker redispatches and retries, (3) commit final charge only for tool executions that contributed to final output, and (4) issue deterministic refunds/credits for cancelled or superseded executions. Also implement quota rebalancing so concurrent requests from the same org can share leftover provisional allocations to avoid hard throttles where possible.

Why now: Increased customer complaints and billing disputes related to rerank/toolcall workloads; rising support overhead and two high-severity chargeback incidents in Q1 2026. This effort ties directly to Redwood's positioning of predictable, economic inference and will materially reduce overbilling incidents and refund volume.
acceptance_criteria: Metering ledger records provisional allocations per-request with unique metering-trace-id for >=98% of rerank+toolcall traffic
Final commit step charges only executed toolcalls that contributed to the final response; speculative/cancelled executions are refunded within 24 hours
Quota rebalancer prevents hard rate-limit failure for 75% of cases where sibling requests have spare provisional allocations (measured in integration tests)
End-to-end integration tests cover redispatch, worker retries, prefetch cancellation, and cross-worker commit paths
Billing dashboards show reconciled provisional vs committed charges and fewer manual refund tickets (target: reduce manual refund volume by 60% in first 30 days)
No customer-facing latency regression >5th percentile token latency by more than 5% when feature toggled on in canary
implementation_notes: Introduce metering-trace-id header propagated through all workers and external toolcall adapters
Add provisional_charge entries to billing ledger on request acceptance (small fixed credit per expected candidate count + estimated toolcall units)

On finalization, worker that produces final result submits a commit record listing contributing executions; billing engine atomically converts provisional charges into committed charges and computes refunds for non-contributing executions
Background reconciliation job that periodically scans provisional entries older than 1h and forces finalize/refund to ensure eventual consistency

Quota rebalancer service runs in the request admission path. It can borrow unused provisional credits from low-priority sibling requests within the same org for short windows, subject to hard safety caps
Instrument more granular metering metrics: provisional_allocated_tokens, provisional_committed_tokens, provisional_refunded_tokens, redispatch_count
Add feature flag gate to enable on org-by-org basis and per-environment (canary/staging/prod)
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger provisional -> commit -> refund transitions including concurrent commit attempts
Integration test that simulates 3 worker redispatches with duplicate toolcalls; assert only one set of toolcall charges is committed
Load test with synthetic rerank workloads to ensure provisional accounting scales and does not introduce bottlenecks
Fault-injection e2e tests where ratecaps cancel in-flight executions and validate refunds and quota rebalancing behavior
QA runbook for manual verification of billing entries and issuance of credits in the sandbox org
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable for internal org + 3 pilot customers. Monitor metering metrics and manual refunds for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (org opt-in): Expose opt-in in Console for customers to toggle redispatchable metering; onboard select early adopters
Phase 3 (gradual default-on): After 6 weeks and meeting metrics targets, flip default-on for all hosted API traffic with realtime monitoring and rollback flag
Fallback: If ledger commit error rate >0.5% or refund latency >24h, auto-disable feature flag and route to legacy metering path while rollback investigations occur
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Ledger race conditions during concurrent commit attempts. Mitigation: use idempotent commit records and optimistic locking with compensating refunds
Risk: Increased billing latency for finalization. Mitigation: keep commit path lightweight; do heavy reconciliation async and ensure provisional credits are visible in Console to prevent confusion
Risk: Abuse of quota rebalancer to bypass org-level rate limits. Mitigation: strict borrowing budgets, audit logs, and anomaly detection on sudden spikes
Risk: Customer confusion about provisional charges. Mitigation: update docs and Console to surface provisional vs committed status and expected refund windows

comments: 2026-02-20 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after two billing incidents were escalated to legal. Initial scope sketched with PM and billing team.
2026-02-25 Marco Nguyen: Added implementation notes for metering-trace-id and provisional ledger entries. Spoke with infra about optimistic locking tradeoffs.
2026-03-02 Leah Cohen (SRE): Asked to ensure background reconciliation job is rate-limited and has backoff; flagged potential datastore hotspots for provisional entries.
2026-03-04 Product review (Daniel Ortiz): Agreed on customer opt-in for Phase 2 and asked for clear Console UX that surfaces provisional credits.
2026-03-06 Engineering review (payment team): Suggested adding a deterministic refund window of 24h and idempotent refund records to avoid duplicate credits.
2026-03-09 Marco Nguyen: Pushed initial schema changes branch to GitHub (PR linked). Unit tests mostly green; integration harness still flaky under high redispatch counts.

2026-03-11 QA (Samira Khan): Found race in ledger commit path when two workers send commit for overlapping contributing executions. Reproduced deterministically in harness. Next: implement idempotent commit guard and rerun tests.

2026-03-13 Marco Nguyen: Mitigation implemented (commit guard added). End-to-end tests passing in staging. Planning canary enablement for internal org next Monday. Follow-up tickets created for Console UX and support docs.
Next steps: schedule canary, finish Console surface (PM ticket PM-4121), and create monitoring dashboards for provisional vs committed metrics
